papers.title_in_file: Quantum Multi-Agent Actor-Critic Neural Networks for Internet-Connected Multi-Robot Coordination in Smart Factory Management
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, simulation setup, results (training and discussion), conclusion; method derivations skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A quantum multi-agent actor-critic framework (QMARL) using variational quantum circuits, evaluated in simulation on a smart factory multi-robot task.

assertions.value: The authors report that in their smart factory simulation the proposed QMARL scheme reached a final total reward of −37, while the comparison schemes Comp1 and Comp2 stayed between −205 and −240, which the authors note is lower than −200, the expected reward of a random walk.
quotes: Then, the total reward of Proposed achieves the final value of −37.
Comp1 and Comp2, which share a common state-value network composed of a small number of parameters, do not evaluate their values properly and cause the reward to exist between −205 and −240.
This is lower than −200, which is the expected value of the total reward when a random walk is performed.
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated environment reported by the authors; empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison schemes are the authors' own baselines in a simulated environment.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the number of qubits used is lower than 110, they assume quantum noise is negligible in their simulations.
quotes: Because the number of qubits used in this paper is lower than 110, this paper assumes that quantum noise is negligible.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own noise assumption in the simulation settings.
assertions.reader_inference: Results are therefore noise-free simulation results, not hardware results.

assertions.value: The authors state in the conclusion that the proposed QMARL has an explicit performance gain over the classical MARL algorithm when using the same number of parameters.
quotes: the proposed QMARL has an explicit performance gain when using the same number of parameters compared to the classical MARL algorithm
assertions.certainty_reason: Author conclusion drawn from their own simulations.

papers.what_it_is: A mathematical physics paper on transparent boundary conditions for the Schrodinger equation on quantum graphs driven by an external potential.
papers.why_not: Quantum graphs here are metric graphs for the Schrodinger equation. The paper has no quantum computing or machine learning workload.

papers.title_in_file: A Comparative Analysis of Hybrid-Quantum Classical Neural Networks
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methodology, results sections IV-B to IV-E, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing QuanNN, QCNN and QResNet hybrid models on a small MNIST subset while varying entangling circuit, layer count and qubit count.

assertions.value: The authors report that in their PennyLane results the QuanNN accuracy converges to around 80% for all three entangling circuit types, with the Strongly Entangling variant highest.
quotes: Towards the end of the training, we can see that the accuracy of the QuanNN, for all three entanglements, converges to around 80%, with the SE QuanNN having the highest accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use a subset of MNIST with only 4 classes, and that they present the Qiskit and PennyLane pipelines separately because cross-tool comparison is out of the scope of the paper.
quotes: we use a subset of the MNIST dataset [15] consisting of only 4 classes
to avoid cross-tool comparison which is out of the scope of this paper
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset and scope in Section IV-A.

assertions.value: The authors state that Qiskit QuanNN and QResNet models show no overall trend with the number of layers, and that their findings suggest the best circuit configuration cannot be identified easily for a given algorithm.
quotes: do not have an overall trend with respect to increasing the number of layers
the best circuit configuration cannot be identified easily for a given algorithm when keeping in mind all the constraints.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation from one study.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking data encoding methods in Quantum Machine Learning

papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, datasets and implementation sections, Malware results, conclusion; other result tables skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation benchmark of five quantum data encodings on four datasets using one quantum neural network classifier.

assertions.value: The authors report that the performance of the encoding methods varies significantly depending on the dataset used and on features of the models.
quotes: The results obtained show that the performance of the encoding methods varies significantly depending on the dataset used and the specific features of the models
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one benchmark study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Malware dataset the highest F1-score is 90%, obtained with Amplitude encoding on 8 features and 4 layers.
quotes: The highest F1-score is 90%, obtained with Amplitude encoding on 8 features, 4 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one benchmark study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations used a single classification model with five feature maps, run on Qiskit simulators, and that benchmarking the best encodings on more than one QNN model is left to another study.
quotes: We carried out our simulations on a single classification model (Figure 1) on five feature maps.
For our simulations, we used Qiskit simulators from IBM
benchmarking them on more than one QNN model
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and a limit in Sections 2 and 4.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Neural Network Inspired Hardware Adaptable Ansatz for Efficient Quantum Simulation of Chemical Systems
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, numerical details, all results sections, conclusion; method derivations skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A VQE wavefunction ansatz (HAA) for quantum chemistry, inspired by quantum neural networks and using ancilla qubits to cut circuit depth, tested by classical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that for BeH2 their test simulations needed at least 25 HEA layers to reach chemical accuracy at all Be-H distances, while an HAA circuit with a single ancilla qubit needed 8 layers.
quotes: We first check the BeH2 system
at least 25 layers are required to reach the chemical accuracy at all Be-H distances. When a single ancilla qubit is available, 8 layers are enough for an HAA circuit to reach the same goal.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 12-qubit HAA simulation of the C9H12 cycloreversion reaction gave an activation energy of 25.79 kcal/mol, which they state agrees well with the experimental results.
quotes: we try to use HAA to study the cycloreversion reaction of cistriscyclopropacyclohexane (C9H12)
Converged results can be obtained by using 12-qubit HAA(2,1) and HAA(2,2) circuits for the reactant and the transition state, respectively.
The obtained activation energy is 25.79 kcal/mol, which agrees well with the experimental results
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.
assertions.reader_inference: The result comes from classical simulation, not a quantum computer run.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQE algorithm was simulated on classical computers using their software Q2Chemistry.
quotes: The VQE algorithm was simulated on classical computers using our homemade software Q2Chemistry
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the numerical details.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Search with Shallow Depth for Unstructured Database Search
papers.version_note: File name says 'Exponential Speedup' (arXiv 2212.09505, earlier version name); the text inside carries the 'Shallow Depth' title, matching the record.
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methods overview, experiment setting, discussion and conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum search algorithm (VQS) that replaces deep Grover circuits with shallow parameterized circuits, tested in noise-free simulation up to 26 qubits.

assertions.value: The authors report that a depth-56 circuit in VQS can replace a depth-270,989 circuit in Grover's algorithm, with experiments up to 26 qubits.
quotes: We demonstrate that a depth-56 circuit in VQS can replace a depth-270,989 circuit in Grover's algorithm.
its exponential advantage over Grover's algorithm in circuit depth for up to 26 qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulation in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the effectiveness of VQS was demonstrated in noise-free simulators, and that the 26-qubit limit is due to the memory of the 48-GB GPU used.
quotes: we have successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of the VQS in noise-free simulators
While this paper has established the advantage of the VQS up to 26 qubits, we acknowledge that this limit is due to the memory capacity restriction of the 48-GB GPU used in our experiments.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limit in the discussion and conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors state that, based on extrapolation from their numerical results, they anticipate VQS may excel beyond 26 qubits, and that numerical verification and mathematical proof for larger qubit counts are future work.
quotes: Based on the extrapolation from the numerical results presented in this paper, we anticipate that the VQS has the potential to excel even beyond 26 qubits.
the next phase will involve numerical verification and mathematical proof of the VQS's scalability for a significantly larger number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Author expectation, stated as not yet verified.
assertions.reader_inference: The exponential-advantage wording rests on noise-free simulation up to 26 qubits.

papers.title_in_file: A New Information Theory of Certainty for Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, experiments (classification and language modeling), quantum troenpy section, discussion; definitions skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of 'troenpy', a certainty measure dual to Shannon entropy, with weighting schemes tested on document classification and LSTM language modeling.

assertions.value: The authors report that in a simple KNN setting their troenpy-based TF-PI weighting gives an average 22.9% error reduction against TF-IDF and an average 26.5% error reduction against HOFTT, across all seven datasets.
quotes: TF-PI very significantly outperforms the classical TF-IDF with an average of 22.9% error reduction and the popular optimal transportation based word moving distance method HOFTT with an average of 26.5% error reduction across all seven datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study by a single author.

assertions.value: The authors report that their troenpy-weighted LSTM lowers perplexity versus the baseline LSTM by about 5 points on PTB and 12 points on the second language-modeling dataset (written WTB in that sentence), averaged over validation and test sets.
quotes: The perplexity reduction is about 5 points for PTB and 12 points for WTB on average over the validation and test datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study by a single author.

assertions.value: The authors define a quantum troenpy as the dual of the Von Neumann entropy, and state that developing its properties is out of the scope of the paper.
quotes: we can define a corresponding quantum troenpy to quantify the certainty of the quantum system
This proposal is obviously out of the scope of this paper and we will investigate on that elsewhere.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope limit in the quantum troenpy section.

papers.title_in_file: An Empirical Study of Bugs in Quantum Machine Learning Frameworks
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, methodology, findings 1 to 4, threats to validity, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of 391 bugs collected from GitHub issue reports of 22 repositories of nine QML frameworks.

assertions.value: The authors report 108 quantum-related bugs, 28% of the 391 bugs studied, with the remaining 72% in the classical part.
quotes: Finding 1. There are 108 quantum-related bugs, accounting for 28% of the total bug count of 391, while the remaining 72% of bugs occur on the classical part.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study with manual classification.

assertions.value: The authors state that they crawled 1,591 issue reports from 22 repositories and manually filtered them to a set of 391 real-world bugs.
quotes: After selecting QML frameworks, we crawled all the issue reports from the 22 repositories above, consisting of 1,591 issue reports.
We collect and inspect a set of 391 real-world bugs from 22 open-source projects
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own data collection scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that they only looked for bugs on GitHub, and that two authors disagreed a lot in bug classification, so a high agreement rate was not reached.
quotes: First, we only look for bugs on GitHub
two authors disagreed a lot in the process of bug classification, which led to the inability to reach a high agreement rate.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own limits in Threats to Validity.
